system.name: Virtuoso
system.one_liner: a simulation framework coupling a lightweight userspace kernel (MimicOS) to architectural simulators for fast, accurate virtual-memory research

components.name: MimicOS
components.role: lightweight userspace kernel that imitates the OS's virtual memory subsystem

components.name: OS Modules
components.role: column of MimicOS's simulated OS functionality modules

components.name: Page Fault Handler
components.role: MimicOS module that processes forwarded events such as page faults (step 3)

components.name: Instrumentation Tool
components.role: dynamically instruments MimicOS's binary to extract disassembled instructions (step 4)

components.name: Communication Interface
components.role: exchanges events and instructions between MimicOS and the architectural simulator

components.name: Architectural Simulator
components.role: existing simulator that Virtuoso is coupled with

components.name: Core Model
components.role: models core execution; receives injected instructions and OS-overhead evaluation

components.name: Memory Model
components.role: models the memory subsystem; source of events such as page faults (step 1)

components.name: Userspace Kernel Instructions
components.role: disassembled MimicOS instructions injected into the instruction stream channel (step 5)

flows.what: a page fault event requiring OS intervention
injects MimicOS's disassembled instructions into the processor performance model
signals the core to restart walking the page table
returns the functional response to the architectural simulator

content.key_idea: Virtuoso couples a lightweight userspace kernel (MimicOS) to an architectural simulator via a shared communication interface, so simulator events like page faults are handled and timed by real OS-like code.
content.reading_order: top-down: MimicOS's OS modules and instrumentation tool first, then through the communication interfaces down to the simulator's core and memory models

encoding.color_means: blue = functional/control channel and events (page fault, restart PTW), red = instruction-stream/instrumentation path, orange = the simulator's core and memory models, dark gray = communication interface boxes, green = qualitative benefit call-outs
encoding.line_style_means: no dashed/solid distinction; all edges are solid, differentiated only by the blue (functional) vs red (instruction-stream) color coding
encoding.emphasis: the 7 numbered steps trace one concrete request end-to-end, and the dual color coding separates the control path from the data/instruction path
reusable_patterns: two-panel host/target diagram bridged by an identically-labeled 'Communication Interface' component in each panel
numbered steps overlaid on a control/data dual-channel diagram

summary: Figure 4 is Virtuoso's own architecture overview, not a background diagram. Virtuoso couples a lightweight userspace kernel, MimicOS, with an existing architectural simulator through a shared 'Communication Interface' component drawn in both panels. MimicOS's OS Modules include a Page Fault Handler and an Instrumentation Tool; the simulator panel holds a Core Model and Memory Model. Seven numbered steps trace one request: a page fault in the Memory Model (1) is forwarded to MimicOS via the functional channel (2), the Page Fault Handler processes it (3), Virtuoso instruments MimicOS's binary (4) and injects disassembled instructions into the Core Model via the Instruction Stream Channel (5), then MimicOS signals a page-table-walk restart (6) and returns its functional response through the functional channel (7). Blue marks the functional path and red marks the instruction-stream path.
